items.text: SCRIPT, a trial led by the universities of Bern and Lucerne with the participating cities, sells cannabis with counselling through pharmacies in the city of Lucerne (and in Bern and Biel). Planned from May 2024 to April 2026, with up to 1,091 participants across the three cities; the federal list still showed it on 3 November 2026.

Under the federal pilot-trial rules, only adults who live in this canton and can show they already use cannabis may enrol. Participants may use the products only themselves: no passing them on and no use in publicly accessible places. Visitors from outside the canton can't enrol or buy, and the national cannabis ban applies to everyone outside the trials. Each trial is limited to five years, with one extension of up to two years possible; the legal basis for the trials ends on 14 May 2031.

Federal-approved cannabis pilot trial here: SCRIPT (Lucerne): non-profit sale in pharmacies with counselling. Pilot trials are scientific studies approved by the federal health office; organisers report to it yearly.

laws.rule: Lucerne charges a cantonal accommodation levy (Beherbergungsabgabe) of CHF 1.10 per person per night (about A$1.90) under the version in force from 1 January 2026; the Regierungsrat may raise it to at most CHF 1.50 (about A$2.59) (§ 9). Hotels, hostels, guest houses, holiday rentals, campsites and caravan sites are covered, including when booked through a third-party platform (§ 7). It is not charged for children under 16, people on official duty, people with tax residence at the place, travellers (Fahrende), and refugees and asylum seekers (§ 8(2)). Communes may add a local levy of up to CHF 1.50 a night (§ 12), and a Kurtaxe in resort areas, with the amount set in the commune's own regulation (§§ 14 and 15). Hosts who give false information or breach reporting duties can be fined up to CHF 10,000 (about A$17,274) (§ 22). AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CHF 0.5789.
